prompt: Put the four quadrants of a spiral turn in order.
trap: Risk comes before building, which is the point of the model.

prompt: What chooses what each turn of the spiral is about?

choices.text: Whichever part is easiest
A fixed schedule of phases
Risk
choices.why: Right: the biggest uncertainty goes first.

choices.text: The next feature on the product owner’s list, in the order she wrote it down
choices.why: That is a backlog order; the spiral orders by risk.

prompt: Why does the lesson call identifying and resolving risks "a testing activity in all but name"?

choices.text: It designs experiments able to refute a belief, like a prototype
Because testers run that quadrant alone
It produces test cases
Because it happens after the code is written, like testing in the waterfall

prompt: Boehm described the spiral as a meta-model. What does that mean?

choices.text: It has no testing
It replaces all other models and makes them obsolete for any kind of project
choices.why: It contains them; it does not abolish them.

choices.text: Each turn takes the shape the risk calls for
choices.why: Right: a small waterfall, an experiment, a piece of a V.

choices.text: It is a model about meetings

prompt: Why did the price rule sit third on Cine Aurora’s risk list, though the course spends eight lessons on it?

choices.text: It does not matter to customers
Prices cannot be tested early
choices.why: A review with Célia is early and cheap.

choices.text: Because Rafael had already tested it thoroughly with dozens of inputs before the list was made
choices.why: Nothing says so, and lesson 1 shows otherwise.

choices.text: It is the cheapest to fix late
choices.why: Right: one function, nothing built on it.

prompt: Lia’s program tried to double-sell a seat a thousand times and never succeeded. What should she say about it?
hint: What an experiment did not show.

choices.text: The risk can be removed from the list
Nothing
choices.why: The result is worth reporting, with its limit.

choices.text: A thousand tries found nothing, which proves nothing about ten thousand

choices.text: Double-selling is impossible
The whole system, rough, then better, then good
One long pass through the phases
No planning at all, with features chosen each morning by whoever arrives first
Each piece finished before the next is built

prompt: Built incrementally, when would Cine Aurora have met the refused orders inflating the seats report?

choices.text: Before the price rule
Late, at integration

choices.text: In the first week

choices.text: Never

prompt: What is the testing risk of purely iterative delivery?

choices.text: Nothing finished enough to test thoroughly, and defects dismissed as drafts
choices.why: Right: its strength is early feedback from Célia.

choices.text: Integration happens too late
Too much documentation
Customers see too much

prompt: Most modern teams combine both. How, by this lesson?

choices.text: Thin end-to-end slices, each grown iteratively
choices.why: Right: one kind of ticket through the whole shop, then wider.

choices.text: Alternating months
One team does incremental work while another team works iteratively on a copy
Using the Rational Unified Process exactly as published
choices.why: RUP was one form; the lesson describes the general combination.

prompt: Checking that what worked before still works after a change is called ___ testing.
The sixty-year-old fix changes `>` to `>=`. Which case does a regression test protect against breaking?

choices.text: The Wednesday price for adults at evening sessions on the cheapest day
choices.why: Possible, and unrelated to this line.

choices.text: Fifty-nine still paying full price
choices.why: Right: a fix that broke fifty-nine would be a new defect.

choices.text: Sixty paying half
choices.why: That is what the fix adds, not what it might break.

choices.text: Nothing: one character cannot break anything

prompt: Why does regression testing become the strongest argument for automation?

choices.text: It finds the most defects
Automation is required by law
Manual testers cannot repeat a test
It grows every turn until, by hand, it is most of the testing time
choices.why: Right: `cases.py` runs six cases in a second.

prompt: "Every defect found should leave a test behind." What does the lesson say those tests become over time?

choices.text: A record of where the system is most likely to break again
choices.why: Right: everything it ever got wrong.

choices.text: A burden to delete each year
choices.why: The lesson argues for keeping them.

choices.text: Proof the system is correct
The specification that replaces the requirements Joana wrote
choices.why: They check against requirements; they do not replace them.
